artboards.title: Provenance — which words became which rule

annotations.text:
The thesis

This isn't a dashboard, it's a trust instrument. Someone has handed an autonomous agent their wallet, and they have three questions in this order: am I safe right now, can I stop it, can I prove what happened.

So the console answers them in that order. A full-width band states the answer — status, money committed, kill switch — before any table appears. Detail lives below it, not above.

The system

Instrument Serif for anything that speaks (status, the sentence, headings); IBM Plex Mono for everything measured. Numbers are tabular throughout.

Colour is signal, never decoration: amber = the model's work, mint = verified by code, coral = refused, indigo = proven by hash. Each zone is introduced by a hairline in its own colour.

The idea worth stealing

Every enforced rule is traced back to the words that produced it. Click a clause, watch its rule light up.

The payoff is the rule that traces back to NOTHING — frequency_cap had no source clause, which is precisely why the compiler flagged it. The provenance view makes an abstract safety property into something you can point at.

The surface everyone forgets

The person who granted the mandate is not sitting at a console. They get plain language — "Wine — you excluded alcohol" — and one unmistakable control.

No fake status bar: that space is left for the real one.
